justifications.functional_suitability: Customer/Broker Portal and Adjuster Workstation support R-01 and R-02. The Claim Router Component enables phased migration (R-03). However, core business processing services for newly migrated claim types are conflated into the routing engine rather than explicit domain services.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The Local Read-Model Cache directly addresses R-05, isolating Adjuster Workstation queries from the 5-second mainframe latency. Asynchronous processing via Azure Service Bus and rate limiting in Azure API Management Gateway prevent mainframe saturation.
justifications.compatibility: The Azure API Management Gateway and Mainframe Proxy Route provide controlled mTLS/ExpressRoute integration with the legacy DB2/COBOL system. Active Directory integration covers authentication. Mechanisms specifically addressing the strict nightly batch window constraint are not explicitly detailed.
justifications.usability: The architecture separates distinct user needs into dedicated frontends: the React Customer/Broker Portal for public self-service and the Angular Adjuster Workstation optimized for high-throughput internal adjuster workflows.
justifications.reliability: R-04 is explicitly satisfied by the Deduplication & State Component enforcing idempotency, paired with the Retry & DLQ Handler Component on Azure Service Bus to prevent claim loss or double processing.
justifications.security: R-07 is fulfilled via Corporate Active Directory and Adjuster Session & Auth Handler (OAuth/OIDC). Key Vault Service, Managed Identity Provider, mTLS, API Gateway Policy Engine, and Audit Trail Ledger provide robust end-to-end security.
justifications.maintainability: The Fallback Switch Component using Azure App Configuration provides rapid one-day rollback per claim type (R-06). Component boundaries are clear, though cloud-native PaaS sprawl may challenge a team with little cloud experience.
justifications.portability: The design satisfies the hybrid deployment brief using ExpressRoute between Azure West Europe and on-premise mainframe. However, it exhibits deep proprietary lock-in to Azure-specific PaaS (Cosmos DB, App Configuration, Service Bus), limiting infrastructure replaceability.

PERF-01.justification: The Local Read-Model Cache enables sub-2s rendering decoupled from the slow mainframe. However, the architecture does not specify how the read-model is populated or kept consistent with mainframe changes.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio and cache synchronization latency
tradeoffs: Read performance vs data eventual consistency

PERF-02.justification: Asynchronous buffering via Azure Service Bus and rate-limiting policies in Azure API Management Gateway absorb submission spikes, preventing overload and shielding the mainframe during the nightly batch window.
sensitivity_points: Message buffering capacity in Azure Service Bus
tradeoffs: Batch protection vs end-to-end processing latency

AVAIL-01.justification: The Integration & Routing Engine uses Azure Service Bus queues and retry handlers to decouple online submissions from the mainframe, reliably holding transactions until the nightly batch window completes.
sensitivity_points: Queue retention limits during extended batch downtime
tradeoffs: Asynchronous store-and-forward vs immediate customer confirmation

AVAIL-02.justification: Cosmos DB deduplication state and dead-letter queues prevent double processing and claim loss. However, half-way failures requiring compensation on the legacy mainframe lack explicit two-way reconciliation logic.
sensitivity_points: Mainframe idempotency support and transaction compensation
tradeoffs: Exactly-once delivery guarantee vs retry overhead and throughput

MOD-01.justification: Azure App Configuration (Fallback Switch Component) combined with the Claim Router enables dynamic claim-type routing and immediate rollback within one day without altering the UI or requiring multiple mainframe changes.
tradeoffs: Routing flexibility vs configuration management complexity

MOD-02.justification: UI and BFF components are decoupled from the mainframe via the integration layer. However, the architecture lacks a comprehensive cloud-native transactional domain store to fully replace the mainframe as system of record.
sensitivity_points: Separation of UI/BFF from backend persistence contracts
tradeoffs: Architectural decoupling vs missing dedicated cloud system-of-record store

SEC-01.justification: The BFF API and Azure AD handle authentication, while audit trails log actions. However, fine-grained object-level authorization (broker-customer boundary validation) is not explicitly detailed in the component definitions.
sensitivity_points: Broker tenant isolation logic in BFF layer
tradeoffs: Centralized authorization enforcement vs portal query performance

SEC-02.justification: Centralized Azure AD integration and session token validation in Adjuster Workstation and API Management enable fast access revocation. Mainframe-side deprovisioning within 15 minutes depends on token lifetime and gateway synchronization.
sensitivity_points: Token expiration window and token revocation propagation
tradeoffs: Fast session invalidation vs frequent token refresh overhead
